title: All 9 Killed After Private Learjet Plunges Into Florida Neighborhood
snippet: A Learjet 60 flying from Texas to the Bahamas crashed into a South Florida neighborhood on Sunday, killing all nine people on board, federal authorities confirmed.
content:
GREENACRES, Fla. — All nine people aboard a private Learjet were killed Sunday afternoon when the aircraft plunged into a South Florida neighborhood in what Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis described as a "cataclysmic" crash.

The aircraft, identified by federal authorities as a Learjet 60, departed from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was en route to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas. According to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), the plane went down around 12:50 p.m. near the intersection of Military Trail and 10th Avenue North in Palm Beach County.

Despite the jet crashing directly into a mobile home community and leaving a crater surrounded by burning debris, authorities reported no injuries or fatalities among residents on the ground.

"We're out of time!" the pilot could be heard saying in chilling air traffic control audio recorded moments before impact. DeSantis, who visited the crash site Sunday evening, noted that witnesses described the jet descending almost vertically, looking "like a missile going down."

NTSB Investigates as Severe Weather Batters Area

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has taken the lead in the investigation alongside the FAA. U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy confirmed the nine fatalities in a public statement Sunday afternoon, calling the crash a "horrific tragedy."

While investigators have not yet determined the official cause of the accident, weather conditions in Palm Beach County were severely degraded at the time. A stalled frontal boundary had triggered widespread thunderstorms across the region, pushing cloud tops tens of thousands of feet high and creating conditions prone to extreme turbulence and severe equipment icing.

Airspace Speculation Dismissed

The location of the crash sparked initial speculation on social media regarding local air defense systems, given that temporary flight restrictions were active for President Donald Trump's visit to his nearby Mar-a-Lago estate. However, federal officials confirmed Sunday night that there is zero indication the aircraft was shot down or interacted with military air defenses.

The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office closed several blocks along Military Trail as emergency crews worked to extinguish scattered fires and secure the extensive debris field. Local utility departments are actively monitoring municipal infrastructure in the surrounding area following the impact.
